title: 09. Production & Safety: Agent Metrics
summary: What are we evaluating? > How well an agent reasons, plans, selects tools, and completes tasks.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
> **What are we evaluating?**
> How well an agent reasons, plans, selects tools, and completes tasks.

sections.title: Task Completion Rate
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TASK COMPLETION = "Did the agent FINISH the task              │
│                     correctly and completely?"                  │
│                                                                 │
│  This is the most important agent metric.                      │
│  Measured by LLM-as-Judge comparing output vs expectation.     │
│                                                                 │
│  SCORING RUBRIC:                                                │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  1.0  Task fully completed, output is perfect            │  │
│  │  0.8  Task done with minor gaps or extra info            │  │
│  │  0.6  Task mostly done, 1-2 key aspects missing          │  │
│  │  0.4  Task partially done, significant gaps              │  │
│  │  0.2  Task barely started, mostly incomplete             │  │
│  │  0.0  Task not attempted or completely wrong             │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                 │
│  EXAMPLE:                                                       │
│  Task: "Find the weather in Tokyo and convert 30°C to °F"      │
│                                                                 │
│  Agent A: "Tokyo weather: 28°C. 30°C = 86°F"                   │
│  → Score: 1.00 ✅ Both subtasks done correctly                 │
│                                                                 │
│  Agent B: "Tokyo weather is warm today."                        │
│  → Score: 0.30 ❌ No conversion done, vague weather            │
│                                                                 │
│  Agent C: "30°C = 86°F"                                         │
│  → Score: 0.50 ⚠️  Only conversion done, missed weather       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Tool Selection Accuracy
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TOOL SELECTION = "Did the agent pick the RIGHT tools?"        │
│                                                                 │
│  Measures: Did the agent call the expected tools?              │
│            Did it avoid calling wrong tools?                    │
│                                                                 │
│  Formula:  F1 of (expected tools ∩ actual tools)               │
│                                                                 │
│  EXAMPLE:                                                       │
│  Task: "Search for Python tips and calculate 2^10"             │
│                                                                 │
│  Expected Tools: [web_search, calculator]                       │
│                                                                 │
│  Case 1: Actual = [web_search, calculator]                      │
│  → Precision=1.0, Recall=1.0, F1=1.00 ✅ Perfect               │
│                                                                 │
│  Case 2: Actual = [web_search]                                  │
│  → Precision=1.0, Recall=0.5, F1=0.67 ⚠️  Missed calculator   │
│                                                                 │
│  Case 3: Actual = [web_search, calculator, database_query]      │
│  → Precision=0.67, Recall=1.0, F1=0.80 ⚠️  Extra tool called  │
│                                                                 │
│  Case 4: Actual = [database_query, email_sender]                │
│  → Precision=0.0, Recall=0.0, F1=0.00 ❌ Completely wrong     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Step Efficiency
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  STEP EFFICIENCY = "Did the agent solve the task in the        │
│                     MINIMUM number of steps?"                   │
│                                                                 │
│  Formula:  min(expected_steps / actual_steps, 1.0)             │
│                                                                 │
│  Task: "What is 2+2?"  (Expected: 1 step)                       │
│                                                                 │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Agent A (1 step):                                       │  │
│  │  1. Use calculator(2+2) → answer                         │  │
│  │  Efficiency = 1/1 = 1.00 ✅ Perfect                      │  │
│  │                                                          │  │
│  │  Agent B (5 steps):                                      │  │
│  │  1. Search web for "2+2"                                 │  │
│  │  2. Search again with different query                    │  │
│  │  3. Use calculator                                       │  │
│  │  4. Verify answer with another calculator call           │  │
│  │  5. Format output                                        │  │
│  │  Efficiency = 1/5 = 0.20 ❌ Very inefficient            │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                 │
│  WHY IT MATTERS:                                                │
│  More steps = more latency, more cost, more failure points.    │
│  An efficient agent = production-ready agent.                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Reasoning Quality
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  REASONING QUALITY = "Was the agent's THOUGHT PROCESS         │
│                        logical and well-structured?"            │
│                                                                 │
│  Evaluates the TRAJECTORY (chain-of-thought), not just output. │
│  Uses LLM-as-Judge to score the reasoning steps.               │
│                                                                 │
│  GOOD TRAJECTORY:                                               │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Think:  "Task is to find population. I'll search."      │  │
│  │  Tool:   web_search("Tokyo population 2024")             │  │
│  │  Observe:"Tokyo population is 13.96 million"             │  │
│  │  Answer: "Tokyo's population is 13.96 million (2024)"    │  │
│  │  Score: 0.95 ✅ Clear, direct, efficient reasoning       │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                 │
│  BAD TRAJECTORY:                                                │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Think:  "I need to find the population..."              │  │
│  │  Tool:   calculator("Tokyo population")  ← WRONG TOOL!  │  │
│  │  Error:  "Expression error"                              │  │
│  │  Think:  "Maybe I should search the web?"                │  │
│  │  Tool:   web_search("weather Tokyo")  ← WRONG QUERY!    │  │
│  │  Think:  "That didn't help, let me try again..."         │  │
│  │  Tool:   web_search("Tokyo population 2024")             │  │
│  │  Score: 0.35 ❌ Confused, wrong tools, wasted steps     │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Agent Metrics Visual Summary
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    AGENT SCORECARD EXAMPLE                      │
│                                                                 │
│  Task: "Search for LangGraph docs, summarize, write Python     │
│         example, and calculate 10! (factorial)"                 │
│                                                                 │
│  Expected tools: [web_search, summarize, execute_code, calc]   │
│  Actual tools:   [web_search, summarize, execute_code, calc]   │
│  Expected steps: 6   Actual steps: 8                            │
│                                                                 │
│  ┌───────────────────────────┬────────┬───────────────────────┐ │
│  │  Metric                   │ Score  │  Verdict              │ │
│  ├───────────────────────────┼────────┼───────────────────────┤ │
│  │  Task Completion          │  0.92  │ ✅ Task done well     │ │
│  │  Tool Selection Accuracy  │  1.00  │ ✅ Right tools        │ │
│  │  Tool Order Accuracy      │  0.95  │ ✅ Correct order      │ │
│  │  Step Efficiency          │  0.75  │ ⚠️  2 extra steps     │ │
│  │  Reasoning Quality        │  0.88  │ ✅ Clear logic        │ │
│  │  Redundancy Score         │  0.90  │ ✅ No redundancy      │ │
│  │  Error Recovery           │  1.00  │ ✅ No errors          │ │
│  ├───────────────────────────┼────────┼───────────────────────┤ │
│  │  OVERALL (weighted)       │  0.89  │ ✅ PASS               │ │
│  └───────────────────────────┴────────┴───────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                 │
│  Action: Optimize step count — 2 extra steps = higher cost.    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
